title: Some Shinkansen Tickets to Increase in Price in 2027
paragraphs: Japan's bullet trains — the Shinkansen — are known for being fast, comfortable and convenient.
But passengers may soon have to pay more to travel on them.
Central Japan Railway Company (JR Central) and West Japan Railway Company (JR West) have announced plans to increase the prices of some tickets in 2027.

The Nozomi and Mizuho trains are Japan's fastest bullet trains, making the fewest stops between their starting and ending stations. During busy periods, passengers can only buy tickets for these trains if they pay for reserved seats.
From July 2027, tickets for reserved seats will increase by between 10 yen — about 6 cents — and 880 yen — about $5.60 — depending on the route.
For example, the route between Tokyo Station and Shin-Osaka Station will increase by 700 yen, or about $4.40. The new price will be 6,510 yen, or about $41.
And reserved seats on the train between Tokyo and Nagoya will increase to 11,880 yen — about $75 — up from 11,300 yen, or about $71.
JR Central and JR West also plan to increase ticket prices for their first-class seats — Green Car seats — in December 2027.

Green Car tickets on Nozomi trains between Tokyo and Shin-Osaka will increase by 3,700 yen, or about $23.40. They'll rise by 4,080 yen, or about $25.70, on Mizuho trains between Shin-Osaka and Hakata.
The companies say the price increases are needed to cover higher operating costs caused by inflation, and to keep making improvements to their services.
